title: Root-algebra localizations along the root divisor are regular
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $f\in R$ have injective multiplication, and suppose $R/(f)$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For $n>0$ put $B=R[T]/(T^n-f)$ and let $t$ be the image of $T$. For every prime ideal $q$ of $B$ containing $t$, the prime localization $B_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. No assumption that $n$ is invertible or that $R$ is regular is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0EYH and 0EYG, local verification over the divisor; Algebra Tag 00NU

proof.text: The positive exponent gives a monic polynomial and the power basis makes B finite free over R. It is Noetherian. Multiplication by f is injective on this free module; t^n=f implies multiplication by t is injective. Localization preserves this injectivity. In Lean, use monic_X_pow_sub_C and Polynomial.Monic.free_adjoinRoot; IsSMulRegular.of_flat and IsSMulRegular.pow_iff give root-coordinate injectivity, and of_flat applies again to the prime localization.

Evaluation at T=0 identifies B/(t) with R/(f), since the relation T^n-f becomes -f. Quotienting B_q by the image of t therefore gives the localization of R/(f) at the prime induced by q. This is regular local by regularity of R/(f). The equivalence is constructed explicitly by AdjoinRoot.lift at zero in R/(f) and the quotient map of the constants in the other direction. Checking their composites on constants and the root proves they are inverse. Map q into B/(t); comap-map and quotient-localization identify the local quotient with the prime localization of B/(t). Transport IsRegularRing across the explicit equivalence, then IsRegularLocalRing across IsLocalization.algEquiv.

The image of t is in the maximal ideal and is a nonzerodivisor. Tag 00NU lifts regularity from its regular local quotient: lift minimal generators of the quotient maximal ideal and adjoin t; the nonzerodivisor dimension formula identifies their number with the dimension of B_q. The private Lean proof lifts a finite set of minimal generators using surjectivity of the quotient map. Adjoin x to these lifts; comap-map proves this set generates the original maximal ideal. Its cardinality is at most the quotient embedding dimension plus one. Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient_span_singleton_succ_eq_ringKrullDim_of_mem_jacobson gives exactly the quotient dimension plus one. Apply of_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_le. No lifting theorem is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem isRegularLocalRing_atPrime_of_root_mem
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (f : R)
    (hf : IsSMulRegular R f) [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (q : Ideal (AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial R) ^ n - Polynomial.C f)))
    [q.IsPrime]
    (ht : AdjoinRoot.root ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial R) ^ n - Polynomial.C f) ∈ q) :
    IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q)
